newsitem.title: USA: Calif. takes legal action against Levitz, GE unit.
newsitem.headline: Calif. takes legal action against Levitz, GE unit.

text.p: The California Department of Insurance said on Monday that it initiated an administrative action against Levitz Furniture and General Electric Capital Corp, a unit of General Electric.

The Department took legal action against the companies for allegedly participating in unfair, or deceptive practices and unfair methods of competition, Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said in a statement.
The Department alleged that Levitz was involved in the illegal sale of credit insurance without a license and that General Electric Capital Corp aided and abetted the company.
A hearing was set for December on the case.

The Department said that Levitz customers unknowingly purchased credit insurance, mistakenly believing that they were only signing up for credit. Although Levitz is not licensed to sell insurance in California, the company sells the credit insurance package in all 34 of its California stores. The credit insurance package includes credit life, disability, involuntary unemployment and property insurance.

The Department said Levitz sells its credit accounts to General Electric Capital, which becomes the true creditor. General Electric Capital charges Levitz a monthly service fee for servicing the credit accounts and provides to Levitz a financial incentive to sell the insurance to customers.
